claim.quote: In this Letter we present the first detection of gravitational lensing B modes, using first-season data from the polarization-sensitive receiver on the South Pole Telescope (SPTpol).

date.note: arXiv v1 submission date; the journal publication date was not read from a fetched source.

name: Detection of B-mode Polarization in the Cosmic Microwave Background with Data from the South Pole Telescope

official_url.quote: Detection of B-mode Polarization in the Cosmic Microwave Background with Data from the South Pole Telescope

significance.quote: We compare this template to the B modes measured directly by SPTpol, finding a non-zero correlation at 7.7 sigma significance.
significance.value: 7.7σ correlation between the SPTpol B modes and a lensing-B-mode template

summary.plain: Using the polarization camera on the South Pole Telescope, the collaboration made the first detection of B-mode polarization produced when gravity bends the Big Bang afterglow, a signal that must be removed to search for inflationary gravitational waves.
summary.technical: SPTpol first season: E modes combined with a Herschel-SPIRE CIB lensing-potential estimate form a lensing B-mode template; correlation with the measured B modes at 7.7 sigma, amplitude and scale dependence as expected.

title: Detection of B-mode Polarization in the Cosmic Microwave Background with Data from the South Pole Telescope
why_it_matters: The abstract says the lensing B-mode signal "provides a measure of the projected mass distribution over the entire observable Universe and also acts as a contaminant for the measurement of primordial gravity-wave signals".
